name: fontSource
summary: Builds one src entry for an @font-face rule, with the right format() beside it.

arguments.name: $font-family
accepts: the family name, which SVG puts in the URL fragment without its spaces

arguments.name: $file-path
accepts: the path without an extension; the format supplies that

arguments.name: $file-formats
accepts: one of eot, woff2, woff, ttf, otf, svg, read in any case
anything else is refused: it used to return an empty list in silence

caveats: Until 4.0.0 a format it did not know fell through both of its branches and the function returned an empty list, so the failure surfaced at the caller's own declaration as Sass's `() isn't a valid CSS value`, naming neither the function nor the format. `font-face` checked its list before calling this and said so in a comment, but a guard that lives only in the caller is not a guard for a public function.

`otf` was missing from `$map-for-font-formats` until 4.0.0, which left a project shipping OpenType with no way to use `font-face` short of restating the whole map, since `@use ... with` replaces a map rather than merging into it. Measured in Chrome 152 and Firefox 156, both keep `format("opentype")` and drop an unknown format word.
